buckets.desc: The base install - team rules, settings core, statusline, and shell shortcuts. Everything else builds on this.

members.desc: Appends the team rules and shared workflow into ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md inside a pair of marker comments, leaving anything you already wrote above and below untouched. Removing this item deletes only the text between those markers.

Adds our permissions, plugins and status-line entry to ~/.claude/settings.json without replacing your own, and puts startup-check.sh, hud.sh and one PATH-repair hook in ~/.claude. It never changes your model or permission mode.

Points ~/.claude/statusline-command.sh at the script that draws the Improv prompt bar: project and directory, git branch with lines changed, model, and context used. It needs jq installed, or the bar just says so and tells you the brew command.

Adds an 'ampersand' function to ~/.zshrc so you can re-run this installer by typing one word from any directory. 'ampersand --pull' updates the repo first, and every other flag is passed straight through. Needs a new terminal, zsh only.

Adds one line to ~/.zshrc that activates your default Node version, so claude, node and npm are found in a brand new terminal. It is skipped with a warning if your ~/.zshrc does not already load nvm, and applies only to terminals opened after.

buckets.desc: Beats is the session-note system that carries context between sessions and machines - the note-keeping rules added to your CLAUDE.md, the /reflect and /consolidate commands, and the checks that keep the notes current. Each part is optional.

members.desc: Adds the note-keeping rules to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, links ~/.claude/startup-check.sh so past notes load at session start, and installs /consolidate for merging related notes. The rules block is rewritten on each install, so edit it in the repo.

Installs /reflect, which reads your accumulated session notes and reports the patterns across them, plus a weekly version and a macOS launch agent in ~/Library/LaunchAgents. That agent is placed but never started, so nothing runs on its own.

Keeps the memory files under .claude/memory guarded, compiled, and fresh as you work. One hook blocks destructive edits to that folder, others compile new entries, warn when they are going stale, and nudge a periodic review.

buckets.label: Sidecoach
buckets.desc: Sidecoach is the design assistant: 26 flows reached by command words such as audit, critique, polish and craft. This group installs the skill, the word lists that match those commands in a prompt, a 'sidecoach' terminal command, and its checks.

members.desc: Builds Sidecoach from the repo and installs the /sidecoach command, the word lists it matches prompts against, and 'sidecoach' plus 'sidecoach-monitor' in ~/.local/bin. Without Node and npm the build fails and the flows will not run.
members.label: Sidecoach

members.desc: Watches for design and UI work as you type, then brings the right context in automatically. One hook spots design intent in a prompt, another injects your project's product and design docs, and a third gates whether a build meets the taste bar before it ships.

buckets.label: Justify
buckets.desc: Justify lets you click an element in your running site and nudge its spacing, type and colour in the browser, then writes the result back into your source. This group installs its server, the /justify command, its terminal tools and its checks.

members.desc: Builds Justify into ~/.claude/justify, adds /justify, registers its tools with Claude Code in ~/.claude.json, and puts eight justify-* commands on your PATH. Needs Node and npm, and a restart of Claude Code before the tools load.
members.label: Justify

members.desc: Keeps the Justify visual-editing loop honest while it runs in the background. One hook guards its source files from accidental edits, one manages the watch process, one reports when it is idle and waiting, one holds the session open until every queued prompt has actually been handled, and one stops any agent from shutting down a justify-* watcher teammate (only you can).

buckets.label: Tiltlab
buckets.desc: Installs the dependencies for the tilt-lab effects workbench inside this repo and puts a 'tilt-lab' command in ~/.local/bin. Nothing runs during install - type 'tilt-lab' to open it at http://localhost:5180 and browse, stack and export effects.
buckets.intro: tilt-lab is the local visual-effects workbench in this repo: browse roughly 25 shader and post-processing effects across four roles (background, midground, pointer, post), stack and tune them live against a real preview, then export the exact stack as a self-contained package. It is the capability Sidecoach reaches for whenever a hero or section wants an animated backdrop.

buckets.label: Lotus
buckets.desc: Builds the Lotus Figma plugin and its bridge inside this repo, adds /lotus, and registers its tools with Claude Code in ~/.claude.json so Claude can edit a Figma file directly. Restart Claude Code, then load lotus/manifest.json once in Figma.
buckets.intro: Lotus is an AI Figma plugin that works directly on the canvas across seven modes - generate, modify, style transfer, components, code export, accessibility audit, and design critique - using whichever AI provider you supply a key for. Its MCP bridge also lets Claude Code read and edit a file's design system in place.

buckets.desc: Reference material Claude can pull in while building an interface - typography, motion, icons, components, platform sizes - plus a check that holds work as unfinished until it matches the Figma file it came from. Each one is optional.

members.desc: Nine reference documents installed under ~/.claude/skills/. Claude opens the relevant one when a task calls for it; they sit dormant otherwise, and each can be installed on its own or in one go with the 'skills' item.

Installs the 16-point checklist for interface detail - optical alignment, hover and focus states, shadow and radius, tabular numbers - plus a companion for reviewing animation. Six files under ~/.claude/skills/tactical-polish/.

Installs a reference that sends Claude to component.gallery to see how established design systems build and name a component before writing a new one. One file under ~/.claude/skills/, and it reads the site only when a task needs it.

Installs a reference so typeface choices start from fontshare.com's curated catalogue rather than defaulting to Google Fonts. One file under ~/.claude/skills/; it recommends fonts and never downloads or installs any.

Installs the working patterns for animation with GSAP and Lenis - scroll-driven effects, page transitions, staggered reveals - and the mistakes that break them. Reference only: your project still has to install GSAP itself.

Installs /curate and creates ~/.claude/design-references/, your own catalogue of interfaces worth copying. A short wizard files each one by category and feel so it can be found later; removing this item keeps the catalogue.

Installs the sizes, safe zones and content rules for 13 platforms, from Instagram and TikTok to Product Hunt and Substack. It tells Claude what a post must fit inside rather than designing one, so it constrains the work instead of doing it.

Installs a way to run a design sprint with 16 named roles across four rounds: research, build, creative-director review, revise. Worth it for a whole page or campaign, and heavy for one component since each role is a separate agent.

Installs 35 files of ready shader and effect source - 14 animated backgrounds, 26 effects applied to images or elements, 17 post-processing passes. All the code ships with it, so nothing is downloaded when Claude reaches for one.

Installs the rules for taking icons from eight approved sets (Heroicons, Lucide, Tabler, Phosphor, Material Symbols and more) by copying their exact shape data instead of drawing one. Pick one set per project, before the first icon goes in.

Holds a Figma-based build to the design it actually came from. The moment a build pulls anything out of Figma, this arms a check that blocks "done" until every pulled element genuinely matches on all three counts: Figma's own value, the code that shipped, and what the live page actually renders.

buckets.desc: Checks that run automatically and stop a mistake before it lands: blocked shell commands, unverified UI claimed as finished, plain-text questions, unsourced assertions, plus browser, Codex and widget checks. A few are pinned always on.

members.desc: Blocks the shell and file-write mistakes that are hardest to undo: a force-push to main, deleting your saved session notes, committing with an AI-attribution line or an outdated model name, or running a command flagged as genuinely destructive, such as a production deploy or one environment's database overwriting another. None of it can be talked past by wording a request differently - the checks match the real command, not what you called it.

Makes "done" mean something was actually looked at, not just built. A code change stays flagged until real proof exists - an opened screenshot, a passing test, a live curl - so a claim that something works can never be taken on faith, and a second edit to the same file within ten minutes gets a warning in case the first fix never really landed. An artifact Claude creates on its own - an image, a page, a document - is held open until it is shown to you.

Makes sure a question aimed at you reaches you as a real, selectable choice rather than buried in a paragraph of chat text - even a plain yes-or-no counts as one. If a plain-text question slips through anyway, the very next message opens with a reminder, since nothing can reach back and fix a reply that has already been sent.

Always-on behavioral discipline with three jobs. Source-grounding checks claims against the real code instead of assumption, completion discipline keeps a task list or prompt queue running to the end instead of stopping early, and response conciseness keeps replies short unless you ask for more, with a toggle to turn it off. A fourth, off by default, rewrites replies for a non-technical stakeholder when you switch it on.

Watches for the tools underneath a session changing without warning - a deprecated flag, a renamed parameter, a service that starts rejecting requests it used to accept. When that happens, it holds the session open until the change has actually been adjusted for, rather than letting things end with a quiet compatibility break nobody noticed.

Three lightweight sanity checks around planning, git, and your own hook install. One reads a written plan against itself and flags outright contradictions, such as a file one section promises that the actual instructions never touch; one reports, at the start of a session, whether the current branch has commits sitting unpushed; and one flags a hook that is present on disk but was never actually written into your live settings, so it looks installed while doing nothing.

Adapts how results are shown to wherever you are actually reading them. A desktop or web session can render real charts and tables and gets nudged toward using them instead of a wall of text; a plain terminal or phone is told to stick to clean markdown, since nothing fancier would render there anyway.

Keeps whichever model you picked from being quietly swapped out from under you. It blocks model-override flags, environment variables, and any per-agent model setting that would route your work to a different model without asking first.

A pure suggestion, never an action: reads what kind of work a message is asking for and names one cheaper specialist agent that could probably handle it. It never actually sends the work anywhere and costs nothing to run, so nothing changes unless you act on the suggestion yourself.

When a session runs on a pricier frontier model (Opus 5, Sonnet 5, or Fable 5), this hands the actual file-writing and shell work to a cheaper preferred model (Opus 4.8 / Sonnet 4.6 / Haiku 4.5) instead, so the frontier model stays in an orchestrating role rather than doing the building itself. It also gates routing a sub-agent onto a frontier model. On the preferred models it does nothing at all - your model choice is never touched. A single typed 'confirm' lifts either gate once.

Two checks around the second-model Codex review step. One reads a finished Codex run for a capacity or connection failure and tells you to retry rather than silently skipping the review it was meant to provide; the other refuses review requests that would fail quietly, such as a helper that can't report its findings back or a request that would just end up reviewing its own work.

Keeps a Chrome tab group from being silently forgotten about. It tracks when browser tabs were last used, only clears that record once closing them is confirmed to have actually worked, and - since a script cannot close a browser tab by itself - holds the session open once if tabs are still open and idle, buying one more turn to close them.

Catches the exact chart and widget mistakes that have shipped invisible text before. Common causes include a hardcoded color where a design token should be, a made-up style variable that does not exist, content wrapped in a tag that breaks rendering, or a font weight heavy enough to look wrong in dark mode.

buckets.desc: Claude speaking its replies aloud, transcribing voice memos you send it, and answering from a Discord channel. Speaking needs your own OpenAI key in the macOS Keychain, Discord needs a bot you own, and transcription runs offline.

members.desc: Puts three Discord scripts in ~/.claude and adds one line to ~/.zshrc, so typing 'claude' offers to connect the session to your Discord bot and you can talk to it from your phone. zsh only, and the bot token is stored in the macOS Keychain.

Installs whisper-cpp and ffmpeg through Homebrew and downloads a 150 MB speech model to ~/.cache/whisper, so Claude can read a voice memo you send it. Runs entirely on your machine with no API key and no audio leaving it.

Claude speaks a one or two sentence summary of each reply out loud, using OpenAI's text-to-speech. This group installs the speech server and the checks that decide when speaking is allowed and track whether you have muted it.

Installs the speech server in ~/.claude/voice-output, registers it with Claude Code, and adds 'voice-on' and 'voice-off' commands to your shell. It arrives muted: run 'voice-on' AND add your own OpenAI key to the Keychain before it speaks.

Controls when the assistant is allowed to speak out loud. One hook gates whether speech fires at all, one carries that decision into the assistant's context so it knows the current state, and one handles you switching voice on or off mid-session.

buckets.desc: Where the work happens - the cmux terminal with the browser pane Claude checks your UI in, a /task-list command for what is next, and a guard on writes to ClickUp. The cmux app itself is a separate download, not installed here.

members.desc: cmux is a split-pane terminal with a built-in browser pane, which is how Claude takes screenshots of your work, and it can show each helper agent in its own pane. This group configures it; the app itself is downloaded separately.

Points ~/.config/cmux/settings.json at this repo's cmux settings, adds a launcher line to ~/.zshrc, and installs ~/.claude/toggle-resume.sh for turning session auto-resume on and off. Auto-resume starts off, and cmux is a separate download.

Keeps cmux's terminal panes and spawned teammates from drifting into a bad state. Hooks here guard against misconfigured panes, heal broken shims automatically, clean up idle teammates that finished their work, and relay a teammate's results back to the session that spawned it.

Installs /task-list, which keeps a plain TASKS.md of what is coming next, with add, list, done, edit, remove, block, unblock and show. It follows the repo you are in and uses that project's file, falling back to a shared list outside one.

Refuses every ClickUp action that would actually change something - creating, updating, deleting, moving, commenting, or tracking time - with no way to confirm past it. Read-only calls such as searching or listing tasks still go through untouched.

buckets.desc: One person's terminal appearance, shown only when the installer is run with --personal. None of it affects Claude Code or your projects; it is Ghostty colours, font and screen effects, so skipping it changes nothing about how sessions behave.

members.desc: Writes the Ghostty terminal appearance (font, 256-colour palette, transparency, blur) into both Ghostty's own settings folder and the copy cmux uses. It is written as a copy, so re-run the installer after editing it, then restart Ghostty.

Clones a community library of Ghostty screen effects to ~/Documents/Github/ghostty-shaders, or updates it if already there. Only the cursor-trail effect is switched on in the config; the CRT and pixel-grid lines are there but commented out.

hook_desc.memory-approve: Auto-approves Write, Edit and MultiEdit into any .claude/memory directory, so saving a session note never stalls on a permission prompt. It only ever grants permission: the write-time content checks still run and can still reject the file.
hook_desc.memory-nudge: Sets a flag when you change a project file and clears it once you save a session note, which is what lets the shell guard hold your commit until the note exists. Read-only commands like git status leave the flag alone; sed -i sets it.
hook_desc.memory-compact: Shrinks the session-notes index right after you edit it, so it cannot outgrow the roughly 24KB loaded into context each session. It ignores every other file and rewrites only when something actually changed.
hook_desc.consolidate-nudge: Counts session notes whose filenames share a topic word and names the largest group once it crosses the threshold, so you can merge them. Advisory only: it never edits or deletes a note, and it waits before raising the same group again.
hook_desc.beats-rebuild: Fires when you save a session note under this repo's .claude/memory and rebuilds the searchable index of those notes in the background. It runs detached and swallows every error, so it can never block or slow your session.
hook_desc.beats-staleness-guard: Checks the session-notes index at startup and acts on the result: a stale index is rebuilt on the spot rather than trusted, a corrupt one raises a loud warning. Silent when it is fresh, and it never fails the session start.
hook_desc.reflect-nudge: Counts the session notes written since your last review and suggests running one when the count passes REFLECT_THRESHOLD, default 15. The first run only records the timestamp, so a fresh machine is never nagged on day one.
hook_desc.sidecoach-keyword: Matches design command words such as audit or polish in your prompt and injects routing for the matching Sidecoach flow. It sanitises first, so one inside a code fence or URL, or a phrase like how do I polish, never fires.
hook_desc.sidecoach-sessionstart: Starts the Sidecoach daemon in the background and writes ~/.claude/.sidecoach-state, which the two sidecoach-post hooks in this list read. It loads no PRODUCT.md or DESIGN.md itself; sidecoach-preamble is what does that.
hook_desc.justify-source-guard: Blocks edits and builds aimed at the installed copy of Justify under ~/.claude/justify, so you change the source in this repo instead. Rebuilding from that stale copy once cut the bundle it serves from 543KB to 291KB.
hook_desc.justify-watch-guard: Prints one informational line at startup when the Justify background watcher is running. It relaunches nothing and never stops you ending a session; the old auto-relaunch caused the very failure it was supposed to prevent.
hook_desc.justify-watcher-guard: Stops any managing, lead, or peer agent from shutting down a Justify-watching teammate (a justify-* watcher). It denies a SendMessage shutdown_request aimed at a justify-* agent and blocks forging the shutdown consent token. Only you can stop a watcher, by running justify-watcher-shutdown in your own terminal. The bare-pid Bash kill of a watcher is blocked by bash-guard; a killed watcher has silently broken the watch before.
hook_desc.justify-watch-standing-by: Corrects the misleading finished label the terminal shows when the Justify watcher is simply parked and waiting. It also drops the watcher's routine idle ping, so Claude does not spend a whole turn answering it.
hook_desc.justify-queue-drain-stop: Stops a session ending while Justify still holds prompts nobody answered. Saying the work is done in chat does not close a prompt, only the justify-done script does, and every other situation lets the session end normally.
hook_desc.agent-teams-guard: Rejects the ways of starting a sub-agent that can never show up as a visible terminal pane: one with no name, one asked to run in the background, and the Workflow tool. It does nothing outside a split-pane team session.
hook_desc.node-shim-heal: Restores the small Node startup file that cmux points NODE_OPTIONS at, which macOS periodically deletes from its temp folder. Once it is missing every node and npx command fails to start, so this replaces it from a permanent copy.
hook_desc.cmux-close-guard: Refuses to close a terminal pane unless nothing is running inside it and you named the exact pane you meant. It was added after a pane closed on a hunch turned out to hold a live worker, killing it and stalling queued work.
hook_desc.cmux-teammate-shim-heal: Replaces the tmux helper that cmux rewrites on every launch with a corrected version. The stock one cannot start a sub-agent pane, because the launch line begins with cd, which it tries to run as a program and fails.
hook_desc.cmux-team-config-heal: Recreates the per-session team folder under ~/.claude/teams when a resumed or upgraded session inherits a team the harness never re-initialized, which otherwise makes every named sub-agent spawn fail with a team-not-found error. It heals the folder from the inherited team name at session start when available, and always from the spawn error itself, so the retry lands without a restart.
hook_desc.team-reaper: Deletes leftover team and task folders under ~/.claude at session start and end, so finished sub-agent groups stop appearing as open workspaces. It skips any group with a process still alive and never touches your notes.
hook_desc.resume-guard: Deletes the saved session files under ~/.nyx/agent-sessions when a session ends, so reopening a terminal tile starts Claude fresh instead of restoring the old conversation. It acts only while ~/.claude/.no-auto-resume exists.
hook_desc.voice-gate: Refuses every text-to-speech call while spoken output is muted, which is whenever ~/.claude/.voice-enabled is missing. Without it a muted session still loads and calls the speak tool, then wastes the turn on a refusal.
hook_desc.block-clickup-writes: Refuses every ClickUp call that would change something: create, update, delete, move, comment and time tracking. There is no way to confirm past it, and read-only calls such as get, list and search go through untouched.
hook_desc.visualizer-guard: Refuses chart or widget code that hardcodes a color inside var(), names a style variable that does not exist such as --text-100, wraps itself in CDATA, or sets font-weight above 500. Each of those once shipped text invisible in dark mode.
hook_desc.codex-failure-watcher: Reads the output of a finished codex command for a capacity or connection error and tells you to retry rather than quietly skip the second-model review. It cannot spot a codex run that hangs, only one that finished badly.
hook_desc.codex-rescue-guard: Refuses two ways of asking the codex helper for a review that fail silently: a named one, which cannot send its findings back, and a review request, which quietly falls back to reviewing its own work. Fix requests still work.
hook_desc.chrome-tabgroup-track: Records that this session has browser tabs open and updates the timestamp on every browser call, so a later check can tell how long ago you used them. Closing a tab is handled elsewhere and deliberately skipped here.
hook_desc.chrome-tabgroup-clear: Watches the result of closing a browser tab and forgets the group only once it reports itself empty, keeping the record while tabs remain. If the result cannot be read it keeps it, since one extra reminder beats leaked tabs.
hook_desc.chrome-tabgroup-stop: Stops the session ending once when browser tabs are still open and the browser has been idle for 90 seconds. A shell script cannot close a browser tab itself, so it buys one more turn in which Claude closes them.
hook_desc.figma-fidelity-stop: Blocks "done" until a build made from a Figma design is proven to match it. Each design element needs an entry in .figma-fidelity.json where the Figma value, the shipped code and a value read from the live page all agree.
hook_desc.figma-fidelity-arm: Switches the Figma match check on the moment a build pulls a design out of Figma, and records which element it pulled. There is no way to opt out: only a matching entry in .figma-fidelity.json turns it off again.
hook_desc.frontier-orchestrator-guard: Blocks file writing and shell commands while an expensive frontier model (Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Fable 5) is running the session, so the actual building is handed to a cheaper preferred model. On the preferred models it does nothing, leaving your choice untouched. A typed 'confirm' lets the frontier model produce once.
hook_desc.bash-guard: Blocks forbidden shell patterns: attribution in a commit, force-push to main, rm against .claude/memory, and legacy model IDs. It also holds your commit when a session note is owed, a screenshot is unread, or work is unverified.
hook_desc.content-guard: Blocks emojis, long dashes, AI attribution lines and outdated model names from being written into any file. It also refuses edits to .figma-fidelity.pending, matched by real location so a symlink cannot get around it.
hook_desc.content-guard-stop: Checks Claude's last chat message, rather than a file, for emojis and long dashes and makes it send the message again cleanly. Chat text is not a file write, so nothing else inspects it before it reaches you.
hook_desc.destructive-ops-guard: Refuses dangerous infrastructure commands outright: deploying to production, copying one environment's database over another, and merging a pull request. Words inside quotes are ignored, so a commit message naming one is safe.
hook_desc.destructive-confirm-detect: Watches for you typing a confirmation word and turns a previously refused dangerous command into a single-use approval. It is the only thing that grants that approval and reacts only to you, so Claude cannot approve itself.
hook_desc.verify-before-done: Arms a verification flag on any code change and clears it only on real proof: a screenshot, a localhost curl, a test run, or reading a probe log. The shell guard reads that same flag to hold your commit until proof exists.
hook_desc.verify-before-done-stop: Stops Claude declaring a visual change finished before it has actually looked at a screenshot. Loading the page, running tests, or fetching a URL do not count; it interrupts once per turn so it can never trap a session.
hook_desc.verify-clear: Counts work as visually checked only after a genuine browser screenshot. Simply loading a page, reading its text, or running a script inside it no longer clears the requirement, a gap that once let a broken UI ship.
hook_desc.verify-manual: Clears this session's outstanding check when you type verified, looks good, lgtm, or bypass verification. The phrase must be your entire message, and it applies only to this session so it cannot excuse another one.
hook_desc.screenshot-open-mandate: Notes the file path each time a screenshot is saved to disk and requires Claude to actually open it. A screenshot that is never opened never appears in your conversation, so describing one only captured is an empty claim.
hook_desc.screenshot-open-clear: Ticks a screenshot off this session's outstanding list the moment Claude opens it, which is the only way that requirement is ever met. The list belongs to one session, so opening a file elsewhere cannot excuse it.
hook_desc.artifact-open-mandate: Notes the path each time Claude creates an artifact worth showing - an image, a page, or an authored document - and requires it to be surfaced to you before the turn ends. Beats, scratch files, source and config files, and internal repo docs are left alone, so only real deliverables ever get flagged.
hook_desc.artifact-open-clear: Ticks an artifact off this session's outstanding list the moment Claude surfaces it, whether by opening it or by publishing it. The list belongs to one session, so surfacing a file elsewhere cannot excuse it.
hook_desc.artifact-open-stop: Blocks the end of a turn once while any artifact Claude made this session is still unshown, listing each one and how to surface it. A file that no longer exists is dropped rather than left to wedge the turn, and once everything is shown the turn ends normally.
hook_desc.artifact-announce-stop: Blocks the end of a turn once when Claude's own closing message tells you a deliverable is at a location (on your desktop, saved to a path) but the file was never opened this session and is sitting closed. It only fires when a real, unopened, non-internal file is named with delivery wording, catching documents a build script created that the creation-time check cannot see.
hook_desc.second-fix-gate: Warns when a second edit hits the same file within ten minutes while an earlier change is still unchecked, the pattern that once turned one bug into a worse one. Edits that only add to existing text are ignored.
hook_desc.validation-guard: Blocks JavaScript that fakes real interaction: getComputedStyle, textContent, element.click, dispatchEvent and similar. Feature detection such as CSS.supports still passes, and the same blocklist is enforced for shell commands.
hook_desc.multiple-choice-detect-stop: Notices when Claude asked you a question as plain text instead of a proper selectable prompt, and records it so the next turn gets a reminder. A plain yes or no counts, since that is simply a two-option question.
hook_desc.multiple-choice-inject-prompt: Delivers that reminder at the start of your next message, before any reply is composed. Nothing can intercept a response before you see it, so correcting the following turn is the only enforcement available.
hook_desc.grounding-gate: Detects a question about why a build behaves as it does, such as why the panel is not showing, and injects a rule to read the code and past session notes first. It also arms the flag that blocks probing the running app before then.
hook_desc.grounding-guard: Refuses screenshot and click tools until Claude has actually opened or searched a file in the same turn. Added after a question about a UI bug was answered by photographing the app rather than reading the line that caused it.
hook_desc.task-loop-mandate: Reminds Claude to finish the whole list of work you gave it instead of stopping partway or asking permission to start something you already approved. It repeats each message, because one reminder at startup fades.
hook_desc.justify-queue-mandate: Re-injects the rule to finish every prompt queued in Justify, the visual review tool. It repeats at session start and briefly on each prompt, and it names the idle heartbeat explicitly so a routine ping is never mistaken for real work.
hook_desc.concise-mandate: Injects the concise-response ruleset each session so replies stay brief. On by default; say "concise off" to stop.
hook_desc.concise-toggle: Turns brevity on or off at runtime - reacts to "concise on", "concise off", "verbose", and "concise status". The command must be your whole message, so those words never fire mid-prose.
hook_desc.concise-detect-stop: Checks the finished response and blocks once when it tacks a new subject on after the closing line or runs a list past five items. It never gates on word count, which would false-fire on every legitimate deep dive.
hook_desc.elias-mandate: Injects the stakeholder ruleset each session so replies are written for a non-technical reader: outcome first, plain language, timeline and risk stated out loud. Off unless you turn it on by saying "elias on".
hook_desc.elias-toggle: Turns stakeholder framing on or off at runtime, reacting to "elias on", "elias off", "stakeholder mode", "technical mode" and "elias status". The command must be your whole message, so those words never fire mid-prose.
hook_desc.elias-detect-stop: Checks the finished reply while stakeholder mode is on and blocks once when it still carries a code block, a file path, a command line or code-shaped names. It judges shape, not vocabulary, so ordinary plain-English explanation passes.
hook_desc.declared-broken-guard: Blocks the end of a turn once when a reply calls a tool or capability dead without having tried to diagnose it that turn. It passes when any check or a differing retry was run, when an outage was cited, or when you were the one who called it broken, so honest dead-ends still get through.
hook_desc.named-tool-swap-arm: Notes when your message tells Claude to use a specific named tool, such as spawning an agent or running a slash command, so the end-of-turn check can tell whether that tool actually ran. It records nothing for ordinary requests.
hook_desc.named-tool-swap-guard: Blocks the end of a turn once when you named a specific tool to use, that tool never ran successfully, and Claude claimed the task done another way without your sign-off. Deliberately narrow, it prefers to stay silent rather than misfire on rewording.
hook_desc.api-drift-detector: Watches tool results for signs an API changed underneath you: deprecated, removed, unknown parameter, or a validation error. Editing a hook, settings.json or a launcher script counts as handling it and clears the warning.
hook_desc.api-drift-stop: Stops the session ending while such an API change is still unhandled. It interrupts only once per turn, skips sub-agents, and clears when you either adjust the affected file or type drift handled.
hook_desc.api-drift-ack: Clears that pending API warning when you type drift handled. It is the manual way out of a false alarm, or of a change you already dealt with by hand.
hook_desc.plan-consistency-lint: Checks a written plan that splits work into sections for contradictions inside itself: a file a section claims but its instructions never mention, or a step marked blocked yet told to start now. It compares the document to itself.
hook_desc.push-ahead-check: Tells you at startup when the current branch has commits you never pushed, naming the branch and how many. It only reports: it never pushes, never blocks, and says nothing outside a git repo or on a branch with no remote.
hook_desc.hook-deploy-currency: Warns at startup when a hook is on disk but was never written into your live settings, so it looks installed while doing nothing. Names the hooks and says to re-run install. It only reports; it stays silent when every installed hook is live.
hook_desc.claude-surface: Works out whether this session can display rich visuals or only text, then tells Claude how to present results. Desktop, web and VS Code get charts and tables; a plain terminal or phone gets clean markdown instead.
hook_desc.surface-visual-gate: On a display that can render visuals, interrupts once when the reply dumps a large table as plain text and asks for a chart instead. Plain terminals are skipped, because a markdown table is the right answer there.
hook_desc.model-router-guard: Stops Claude quietly moving your work to a different model, blocking model override flags, model environment variables and per-sub-agent model settings. There is no override: the model you picked is the one that runs.
hook_desc.route-intent: Reads what kind of work your message asks for and names one cheaper specialist agent that could handle it. It is a suggestion only: it never sends the work anywhere, costs nothing to run, and stays quiet on short messages.
hook_desc.resume-toggle: Turns terminal auto-resume on or off when you type resume on, resume off, resume toggle or resume status. It only writes the flag at ~/.claude/.no-auto-resume; a separate entry in this list clears the saved sessions.
hook_desc.teammate-relay-stop: Stops a sub-agent finishing quietly when it was told to send its report back and never did. It reads only real instructions, so a tool result that merely prints the word SendMessage cannot set it off.
hook_desc.sidecoach-preamble: Injects your PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md into context at session start and whenever the conversation is compacted, so design constraints hold even when you never ask for a review. Each file must exceed 200 chars and carry no TODO marker.
hook_desc.sidecoach-postuserp: Passes your message to the Sidecoach background service. It exits immediately when that service is not running, and gives up after one second, so a stalled service can never hold up your turn.
hook_desc.sidecoach-taste-gate: Scans every .html or .css file you save inside a project that has a DESIGN.md, checking for banned visual patterns and, on HTML, a wider quality pass. It cannot catch anything needing the page rendered, such as low contrast.
hook_desc.sidecoach-orchestrate-edit: On a substantive design-file edit it runs the headless defect scan and injects the audit, critique and polish QA gate, so the orchestrator engages without you loading a skill or typing a verb. Advisory, never blocks, and stays quiet for a cooldown window after it fires once.
hook_desc.sidecoach-qa-gate-stop: Stops Claude declaring a design change finished until the sidecoach QA gate has actually run on it - all three of audit, critique and polish, as real sidecoach runs. Describing the review in prose does not count. Clears on its own once the review runs or the changed files are reverted, and interrupts once per change so it can never trap a session; reply qa done or skip qa to override.
hook_desc.qa-gate-manual: Clears this session's outstanding sidecoach QA-gate check when you type qa done, skip qa, qa override, gate override, looks good, or verified. The phrase must be your entire message, and it applies only to this session.
hook_desc.sidecoach-craft-floor: Loads a standing UI quality baseline before any interface file is written or edited: 15 rules with concrete values and 10 banned patterns, each naming what to do instead. Fires on any UI edit, at most once every 15 minutes per project.
hook_desc.sidecoach-postresponse: Prints the newest result from the Sidecoach background service at the end of a reply. A failed or inconclusive review is shown rather than hidden, and the result file is removed once it has been displayed.
hook_desc.sidecoach-detect: Runs the full interface defect scanner over each UI file you save and reports what it finds. It only advises, never blocks, is off unless you turn it on, and a scan that could not run says so instead of reporting clean.
hook_desc.sidecoach-heal: Repairs Sidecoach's own wiring at the start of each session: re-creates any missing hook symlink so it resolves and fires, and re-adds any registration that was stripped from settings.json. It only adds, never removes, and stays silent when nothing needs fixing.
hook_desc.voice-mandate: Decides at the start of each session whether spoken output may be used, based on whether it is installed and whether you muted it. It says one of three things: allowed, muted, or nothing at all when it is not installed.
hook_desc.voice-toggle: Switches spoken output on or off when you type voice on, voice off, voice toggle or voice status. It writes the flag at ~/.claude/.voice-enabled, which the other two voice entries in this list read to decide what is allowed.
hook_desc.plugin-node-hook-heal: Points any plugin hook that starts Node by bare name at Node's full location instead. cmux-launched sessions give hooks a stripped-down search path with no Node on it, so those hooks were silently failing every time (the Codex end-of-session review among them). Re-applies itself each session so a plugin update cannot quietly undo it.
hook_desc.sidecoach-taste-promote-arm: Mints the single-use taste-rule promotion consent token when you type, as your whole prompt, "promote-confirm <candidateId> <store> <digest>" (the digest, from approve/show, binds the approval to the reviewed content). Nothing else arms it, and an agent cannot submit a prompt, so only your typed confirm can approve promoting a mined taste rule into the guidance store.
hook_desc.sidecoach-taste-enforce-arm: Mints the single-use taste-rule ENFORCE consent token when you type, as your whole prompt, "enforce-confirm <ruleId> <precision-digest>" (the digest, from the enforce approve helper, binds your sign-off to a fresh held-out precision measurement). Nothing else arms it, and an agent cannot submit a prompt, so only your typed confirm can flip a mined taste rule from advisory guidance into a build-blocking detector.
hook_desc.taste-blocking-toggle: The global master switch for live taste blocking. Type "taste blocking on", "taste blocking off", "taste blocking toggle" or "taste blocking status" and it flips the flag at ~/.claude/.taste-blocking-enabled. Default is OFF (advisory): a certified machine-learned rule warns but never blocks, so it can never block a faithful implementation of an approved design. Turn it on only when you want enforcement.
hook_desc.taste-blocking-status: Announces the current taste-blocking mode at the start of each session, reading the same flag the toggle writes. It only reports; it never blocks. OFF (the default) means certified mined rules stay advisory; ON means they block the build and gate when they fire.

hook_note.model-router-guard: Recommendation: designed to keep Anthropic from routing away from Fable 5 if erroneously detects unsafe behavior, but prevents Claude from routing agents based on LOE. Do not activate.

hook_data_excluded.cluster-wirings.json: installer wiring table, read by install.sh - not a runtime hook companion
